summary: Add customer_note column via ALTER TABLE, backfill existing note values, deploy new-staged version skipping Django column-creation migration, retire old app, then drop note column.
write_consistency: Backfill synchronises note → customer_note for all rows. During concurrent phase old app writes to note and new app writes to customer_note. After retire_old only new app runs, which exclusively uses customer_note. The note column is removed only after old app retirement, guaranteeing no write conflicts and that the old column is gone at the end.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed at deploy_new because Django's migration registry was unaware of the customer_note column added by raw ALTER TABLE in the expand stage. When deploy_new ran with `migration: "apply"`, Django attempted to CREATE the column again and halted with ProgrammingError. This revision sets `migration: "skip"` in the deploy_new stage, avoiding the duplicate column creation since the column already exists from expand/backfill SQL stages. The stage ordering (expand → backfill → deploy_new → retire_old → contract) ensures the old app is retired before the note column is dropped, satisfying the retirement gate and preserving data consistency.

stages.description: Add the customer_note column to account_user.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy note values into customer_note for all existing rows.
Deploy the new‑staged version of Saleor; its code references customer_note instead of note. Django migration is skipped because the column already exists from expand/backfill stages.
Retire the old app version; after this only the new app runs, which exclusively uses customer_note.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
